channel.title: Silver Score
channel.description: Two of us, one couch, honest scores — about 8,500+ hours logged, fifteen years of ratings on IMDb-backed titles.

item.title: Essay: Why We Rewatch Michael Mann
item.description: Nobody films people who take their work seriously like Michael Mann — professionalism as drama, cities as pressure, and a shelf we keep revisiting together.

item.title: Essay: How We Find Under-the-Radar Gems
item.description: Under the radar isn't marketing — it's our rule. We rate 8+ while fewer than 50k people have voted on IMDb. That's where most of our favourites live.

item.title: Essay: Subtitles, Dubbing, and What Gets Lost
item.description: Dubbing swaps an actor's voice for a session performer. Subtitles ask a little work and give you back what the director actually shot.

item.title: Essay: The Limited Series Is the New Prestige Film
item.description: Six to eight episodes absorbed the craft energy mid-budget prestige film used to own — where directors and actors go to say one big thing well.

item.title: Essay: The French Polar — Noir That Never Quit
item.description: France never stopped its noir tradition — from Melville through Spiral and Le Bureau des Légendes, while Hollywood kept rediscovering the same thing.

item.title: New list: International Thrillers — Beyond English
item.description: The best tension doesn't need a shared language — thrillers from France, Germany, Israel, India, and beyond. Subtitles are a small price for this quality.

item.title: New list: Slow Burns Worth the Patience
item.description: Stories that trust us enough to take their time — tension from craft, not jump cuts. Worth every quiet minute.

item.title: New list: Korean Cinema — Sharp Edges
item.description: Revenge, class tension, and genre-bending Hollywood still studies — the Korean titles we rate highest and would put on for each other.

item.title: New list: War Films That Earned It
item.description: No glory montages — war that costs something, told with craft, restraint, and respect for what happened.

item.title: New list: Italian Crime — No Heroes Allowed
item.description: Naples, Rome, Calabria — Italian crime where the system is the villain and nobody gets a clean redemption arc.

item.title: Essay: In Defence of Slow Burns
item.description: Why the best thrillers make you wait — a case for patience, quiet tension, and stories that trust the audience.

item.title: Essay: The Craft of Spy TV
item.description: From The Bureau to Slow Horses — what separates great spy TV from action shows in trench coats. Tradecraft, paranoia, and the cost of loyalty.

item.title: Essay: Why Nordic Noir Works
item.description: Landscape as character, silence as dialogue, and detectives who carry the case home — what makes Scandinavian crime different, and why we keep coming back.

item.title: Curated list: Prestige TV That Earned the Label
item.description: Series that earned the late nights — sharp writing, high craft, and finales we still argue about on the couch.

item.title: Curated list: Spy & Thriller Escape Room
item.description: Agencies, aliases, and anxiety — the shows we queue when we want people scary-good at hard jobs, with real stakes.

item.title: Curated list: Nordic Noir & Neighbours
item.description: Slow-burn crime from the north — moral grey zones, landscapes that feel like characters, and detectives who look tired in the right way.
